meta.name: ActivityPageHeader
meta.description: Compact mobile navigation for campaign and editorial landing pages with the approved YAMI lockup, a page title, search and cart actions.

figma.notes: YAMI UI/UX Guidelines H5 Page8 mobile navigation. The supplied node defines only the 402x56 mobile form.

title.description: Short campaign or page title, truncated to one centered line.

locale.description: Content locale. Mobile navigation keeps the approved English YAMI Logo-UI lockup in every locale.

homeHref.description: Optional home destination for the brand lockup.

brand.note: Consumes the locked Mobile Logo-UI assets; the mark and wordmark are never assembled in code.

focus.note: Brand and action controls use the shared token-backed focus ring.

tapTarget.note: Figma's 40px visible actions retain a 44px hit area.

accessibility.role: banner with page heading and two named actions
accessibility.ariaPattern: native h1 plus named search and cart buttons
accessibility.structure: The one-line visible title is the page h1. Icons are decorative inside explicitly named buttons.
accessibility.interaction: Search and cart are native buttons with visible focus treatment.

meta.name: AspectRatio
meta.description: Style-neutral layout primitive that constrains arbitrary content to a caller-provided width-to-height ratio.

ratio.description: Width divided by height, for example 1 or 16 / 9.

children.description: Content constrained by the ratio container.

accessibility.role: none
accessibility.ariaPattern: none
accessibility.notes: Layout-only wrapper. Accessibility semantics belong to its children.

meta.name: Badge
meta.description: Small label for product status, promotion, and counts. Supports sm and md sizes, abstract color × emphasis, four background-polarity tones, and semantic `type` shortcuts matching Figma.

figma.notes: Primary binding is Badge / PC. Both Figma bindings map to the default sm size; md is a code-defined extension. The 4 specialty sets (Top Seller, Membership tag/icon, Badge icon) are out-of-scope for the abstract Badge — track them as separate components if they ship to product.
figma.sizeDelta: Badge sizes are breakpoint-independent: sm is 20px high with 12/16 type; md is 24px high with 14/20 type.

color.description: Semantic color. 'red' only for promotion/sale (rule: red-usage).

emphasis.description: 'primary' = solid bg, high contrast. 'secondary' = tinted bg, softer.

size.description: Breakpoint-independent geometry with 8px horizontal padding. 'sm' = 20px height with 12/16 type; 'md' = 24px height with 14/20 type.

tone.description: Optional background-polarity treatment. Filled tones use translucent black or white; outline tones use a transparent fill and 1px inset stroke. Tone takes visual priority without changing Badge size or radius.

type.description: Semantic shortcut mirroring Figma's Type variant. Resolves to a (color, emphasis) preset (e.g. 'sale' → red+secondary). Explicit color / emphasis props override the preset. 'exclusive' (purple flag) and 'choice' (blue flag) additionally render a flush-left YAMI logo flag prefix matching assets/badges/flag-cap-{purple,blue}.svg.

children.description: Label text. Typically 1 word or short phrase (NEW, SALE, –30%, 限时).

colorUsage.note: color='red' only for promotion / urgency / sale. Never decorative.

semanticColor.note: The 6-color palette IS the sanctioned non-brand color set — this is the one place blue/green/purple/yellow are OK.

noEmoji.note: Badge text is plain. Do not encode pictograms as emoji or as ad-hoc Badge variants.

numerals.note: Digits (–30%, 1.2k, etc.) render in var(--font-family-ios) = GT Walsheim.

surfaceTone.note: Use dark tones on light or mixed backgrounds and light tones on dark backgrounds. All four tones retain the selected Badge size and 4px radius.

accessibility.role: implicit (span)
accessibility.ariaPattern: label
accessibility.notes: Badge is a visual label (non-interactive — tapTargetMin=0). If it conveys state not present in adjacent text (e.g. 'OUT OF STOCK' on an otherwise normal-looking product), ensure the state is also encoded in markup — e.g. aria-label on the parent product element.

meta.name: Billboard
meta.description: Full-bleed promotional band whose entire content is one campaign image, wrapped in a single link.

figma.notes: Modelled on the production yami.com homepage floating bar, which renders a 1585x160 artwork directly under the shortcut rail.

image.description: Campaign artwork with its intrinsic `width`/`height`, which reserve the band's height before it loads. `mobile` swaps in narrow artwork below 1024px, carrying its own dimensions. `alt` is usually empty because `label` already names the offer.

label.description: Localized accessible name. Required: the artwork's words are pixels, so without it the band is an unnamed link.

imageLoading.description: Artwork loading strategy; eager for a band above the fold.

focus.note: The link carries a token-backed focus ring at the band's radius.

radius.note: Consumes --radius-surface-default, matching the other homepage section cards.

tapTarget.note: The whole band is the target, far above the 44px minimum.

accessibility.role: labelled region containing a single link
accessibility.ariaPattern: section[aria-label] wrapping one a[aria-label] around decorative artwork
accessibility.structure: The label names both the region and the link inside it. Naming only the region leaves the link nameless, since its only content is artwork with empty alt and a link takes its name from its content.
accessibility.interaction: One link covers the band; there is no secondary target.

meta.name: BrandProductRail
meta.description: Responsive brand-led commerce rail composed from ProductList, compact ProductCard, and shared rail navigation controls.

figma.notes: PC behavior follows the YAMI homepage reference; mobile behavior follows the Figma brand-mobile / campaign composition.

title.description: Visible section heading and accessible label.

mobileTitle.description: Optional mobile-only section heading; falls back to title.

titleFontFamily.description: Optional serif treatment for editorial section headings.

campaigns.description: Ordered brand campaigns with a banner and ProductList items.

mobileSurface.description: Mobile section surface. Plain is full-bleed with 16px content padding and supports section dividers.

tabs.description: Optional mobile category tabs composed with the existing tertiary Tabs.

defaultValue.description: Initial uncontrolled mobile category tab value.

viewAllHref.description: Destination for the optional view-all link.

previousLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the previous-page button.

nextLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the next-page button.

onAddToCart.description: Reports the campaign and product IDs from the reused ProductCard quick-add action.

dividerPosition.description: Places the section boundary above, below, or removes it; card mobile ignores it while plain mobile preserves it.

dividerVariant.description: Gray preserves the existing 1px structural separator; black uses the theme-aware 2px emphasis separator.

tapTarget.note: Paging and quick-add actions compose existing YAMI Button controls.

focus.note: Campaign, product, view-all, and paging controls retain token-backed focus rings.

--color-white-1000.selector: brand banner title and compact ProductCard image surfaces

--space-600.property: desktop section padding and responsive panel gap calculation

accessibility.role: labelled section containing a horizontally scrollable list of brand campaigns
accessibility.ariaPattern: section with heading, list/listitem campaign panels, links, and previous/next buttons
accessibility.structure: The visible heading labels the section. Each campaign composes a labelled ProductList containing ProductCard articles.
accessibility.interaction: Native horizontal scrolling remains available; desktop paging buttons report disabled edge states.

meta.name: Button
meta.description: YAMI primary interactive element. 4 hierarchies (emphasis / primary / secondary / tertiary) × 3 form modes (full / inline / icon) × 3 sizes (sm / md / lg) × default & inverse surfaces. Mirrors the YAMI UI/UX Guidelines Figma file (Mobile v2 + PC v2).

figma.notes: Primary binding is PC Full-Default. componentKey populated during Phase 10 Code Connect publish. Full node mapping in `figma.nodes` below — each Form × Surface lives in its own component_set because Figma encodes Form via separate sets rather than a variant property.
figma.sizeDelta: Per-form size coverage in Figma: Full + Inline ship Size=Medium (40) and Size=Large (Mobile 48 / PC 56). Icon ships Size=Small (32) / Medium (40) / Large (48 on both Mobile + PC — does NOT bump to 56). Code unifies the size axis to sm/md/lg across all forms; Full/Inline 'sm' is a YAMI-product extension beyond Figma. CSS scopes the lg→56 desktop bump to :not(.iconOnly) so Icon Large stays 48×48.
figma.stateMapping: Figma 'Hover / Active' collapses to two CSS states (:hover + :active) which already share the same `-active` token. Figma omits :focus-visible (a11y-only) and code adds it per rule `focus-style`.

variant.description: Visual role. 'emphasis' is rate-limited to 1 per screen (see rules.emphasis).

leftIcon.description: Prefer SVGs from assets/icons/ which already use currentColor.

form.description: Layout mode mirroring Figma's Form axis. 'full' stretches to container width (replaces legacy fullWidth=true). 'inline' is content-width (default). 'icon' is square, no label (replaces legacy iconOnly=true, requires aria-label). When omitted, derived from legacy iconOnly / fullWidth for backward compat.

inverse.description: When true, swaps to the *-inverse token set for the active theme's opposite-polarity surface. Mirrors Figma's '<Form> - Inverse' component sets.

iconOnly.description: DEPRECATED — use form='icon'. Kept for backward compat (mapped to form='icon' when set). REQUIRES aria-label.

fullWidth.description: DEPRECATED — use form='full'. Kept for backward compat (mapped to form='full' when set).

loading.description: Replaces visuals with a spinner and sets aria-busy.

children.description: Label text; icon node if iconOnly=true.

aria-label.description: Dev-time console warning if iconOnly without aria-label.

useWhen: Primary CTA on a page (Buy Now, Add to Cart, Place Order)
avoidWhen: Secondary actions next to a primary

tapTarget.note: All sizes (sm=32, md=40, lg=48) include padding that expands the touch region to ≥44pt even when visible height is smaller.

focus.note: 2px solid var(--border-focus) ring with 2px outline-offset. Never browser default.

disabledState.note: Uses --button-disabled background + --text-disabled foreground. Never CSS opacity.

radii.note: All full-form buttons → --radius-component-default (8px). Inline buttons → --radius-button-primary (pill) across every hierarchy. Icon form keeps its hierarchy-specific radius.

accessibility.role: button
accessibility.ariaPattern: button

meta.name: Card
meta.description: Surface primitive for grouping related content. No border by default (rule card-no-border), 12px radius, no shadow. Polymorphic via `as` prop (div / a / button) for link and button cards.

as.description: Polymorphic element. Use 'a' with href for link cards, 'button' for button cards.

padding.description: Inner padding tier. 'none' for image-only cards where the img is edge-to-edge.

bordered.description: Opt-in hairline border. Only for dense listing grids — use sparingly (rule card-no-border default).

interactive.description: Adds hover + focus-visible styling. Auto-inferred when as='button' or as='a' + href.

border.note: Default border: none. `bordered` only in dense grids.

elevationOnPress.note: interactive cards change background-color on hover; Card has no elevation API because Figma provides no elevation token source.

focus.note: Interactive cards show 2px --border-focus outline + 2px offset.

accessibility.role: implicit (div, or button/link when as= overridden)
accessibility.ariaPattern: group (default) | button (as='button') | link (as='a' with href)
accessibility.notes: tapTargetMin/keyboardNav apply only when interactive=true (auto-inferred via as='button' or as='a'+href). Non-interactive cards effectively have tapTargetMin=0 and keyboardNav=[]. interactive=true adds focus-visible outline.

meta.name: Checkbox
meta.description: YAMI neutral multi-select control from the Forms Figma page. Uses Base UI for keyboard, ARIA, controlled/uncontrolled state, and native form participation.

figma.notes: The visible component is 20x20 with a 24x24 pointer target.
figma.stateMapping: Status=Default/Hover/Selected/Disable_Selected/Disable_Unselected maps to unchecked hover, checked, checked+disabled, and unchecked+disabled. Indeterminate is code-only.

defaultChecked.description: Initial selected state for uncontrolled use.

onCheckedChange.description: Called when an enabled checkbox changes.

indeterminate.description: Mixed selection state for parent/group controls; code-side extension beyond the Figma set.

focus.note: Uses a 2px --border-focus ring with 2px offset.

disabled.note: Disabled states use --fill-disabled and semantic background colors.

radii.note: Visible square uses --radius-tag-primary for a 4px radius.

tapTarget.note: 20px component with an invisible 2px extension on every side, producing a 24px pointer target. Parent labels may provide a larger target.

color.note: Selected state is neutral --text-primary, not operational or brand red.

accessibility.role: checkbox
accessibility.ariaPattern: checkbox
accessibility.notes: Base UI renders role=checkbox plus a hidden native form input. Provide a visible label or aria-label.

meta.name: Divider
meta.description: Hairline separator (1px). 3 strengths per design.md border-strength rule, plus inverse variants for opposite-polarity surfaces. Horizontal renders as <hr>, vertical as <span role="separator">.

strength.description: Border-strength tier. default=8% / subtle=29% / emphasis=87% (+ inverse variants for opposite-polarity surfaces).

borderStrength.note: Only 3 strengths exist — no arbitrary opacities. Pick default for most cases.

accessibility.role: separator
accessibility.ariaPattern: separator
accessibility.notes: Non-interactive — tapTargetMin=0, keyboardNav=[]. <hr> is inherently role=separator. Vertical variant sets role+aria-orientation manually.

meta.name: FilterChip
meta.description: Interactive 36px filter-pill family with filled and outlined variants, optional icons, single-, multiple-, and hierarchical category popovers, and horizontally scrollable grouping.

figma.notes: Filter popup geometry and selection patterns follow English Site Optimization 2026 nodes 1123:65336 and 1252:78302. Distinct from the non-interactive Tag component.

variant.description: Filled suggested-filter treatment or outlined toolbar-control treatment.

selected.description: Exposes aria-pressed and applies a 1px selected stroke that increases to 2px on hover.

rightIcon.description: Optional trailing icon, commonly the 12px arrow-down asset.

interaction.note: FilterChip renders a button; FilterChipMenu uses Base UI Popover with Checkbox or RadioGroup semantics.

focus.note: Uses a 2px --border-focus outline with 2px offset.

color.note: Surfaces, borders, text, and interaction states use semantic tokens.

accessibility.role: button / radio group / checkbox group supplied by consumer
accessibility.ariaPattern: toggle button trigger with RadioGroup or Checkbox controls in popup
accessibility.notes: Provide accessible labels for chip groups and popup menus.

meta.name: Footer
meta.description: YAMI PC global site footer: a responsive masthead matching the 1920, 1440, and 1024px Figma variants, closed by an inverse bar carrying payment marks, copyright, and legal links. PC only — the mobile footer ships separately.

figma.notes: Geometry and token bindings were verified against the Figma Footer variants at 1920px (6970:69276), 1440px (6970:69581), and 1024px (6970:69886). The 1024px variant stacks the link panel above two side-by-side right bands; 1440px uses a two-by-two link grid; 1920px uses four link columns. The PC footer has a 1024px minimum width and scrolls horizontally below that viewport. The closing payment/legal bar is a fixed dark brand surface and remains unchanged when the surrounding page switches to dark mode. Mobile footer is out of scope for 0.x and gets its own node binding when it ships.

columns.description: Masthead columns in display order. The Figma PC fixture supplies four visual columns; the last column owns the Make Money and Contact groups.

subscribe.description: Newsletter block: heading, field labelling, submit label, and optional controlled value. Omit to drop the whole keep-in-touch band. Email validation is deliberately the caller's concern — the DS surfaces `error` and fires `onSubmit`.

socialLinks.description: Social follow entries rendered above the newsletter field. Glyphs come from assets/icons/social/ and are decorative — each anchor names itself via its label.

appTitle.description: Heading for the app band, e.g. "Shop on the go. Get the app."

appLinks.description: App-store download entries, rendered as FooterAppButton. Badge artwork remains caller-supplied; the fixture uses the maintained 24px Apple and Google Play marks.

copyright.description: Copyright copy rendered in the closing bar, either as one line or as the Figma four-paragraph form.

legalLinks.description: Legal entries beside the copyright line. `ariaLabel` overrides the accessible name where the visible label under-describes the target, as production's Business license does.

paymentMarks.description: Accepted payment marks above the copyright line. Artwork carries the scheme name as alt because no visible label repeats it.

ariaLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the contentinfo landmark.

socialLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the social follow list.

legalLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the legal link list.

paymentLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the payment mark list.

semanticColorOnly.note: No raw hue is baked into the CSS. The content panels resolve to --surface-secondary, the input uses --surface-primary, the app controls use the active --surface-inverse, and the closing bar locally binds its inverse semantic tokens to the fixed dark/light-text brand polarity.

typeHierarchy.note: Four levels: heading-2xl (side-band titles), heading-sm (group titles), link-md (column links, field, submit), caption-md (copyright and legal). Production sets group titles at 16/24; the DS pairs 16px with --line-height-heading-sm (20px) because there is no 16/24 slot.

noCustomRadii.note: Only semantic radius slots. Production's 2px input and 4px app button both map to --radius-component-default (8px).

borderStrength.note: The component follows Figma's hierarchy: a default 2px --divider-emphasis top border caps the footer, while 1px --divider-default gaps separate masthead panels and the two right bands. The input ring maps to --border-default.

tapTarget.note: Column links (20px rows) and social glyphs (24px) both sit below 44px. Each keeps its visual size and gains a transparent hit area, as in Header. App buttons and the newsletter field are already 40px tall and 246px wide.

focus.note: Column links, the social links, newsletter submit, app buttons, and legal links expose a 2px outline at 2px offset. The newsletter field reuses its border with --border-focus while focused instead of adding a second ring. Slots on the inverse surface switch to --border-focus-inverse.

redUsage.note: The newsletter submit is the only red in the landmark and uses --text-emphasis, matching production's #e00 text button. Validation copy uses --text-error.

numeralsFont.note: The support phone number and copyright years inherit --font-family-ios from the footer root.

elevationOnPress.note: Hover changes color only — no shadow anywhere in the landmark, matching production.

accessibility.role: contentinfo landmark containing labelled link lists and a newsletter form
accessibility.ariaPattern: footer contentinfo + h3-titled link lists + a form with a visually hidden label; social, legal, and payment lists each carry an accessible name
accessibility.structure: Group titles are real h3 headings so the footer is navigable by heading. Social glyphs are decorative (empty alt) and their anchors name themselves via aria-label. Payment marks carry the scheme name as alt because no visible label repeats it. Legal entries may override their accessible name via ariaLabel where the visible label under-describes the target.
accessibility.interaction: The newsletter field reports rejection through aria-invalid plus an aria-describedby error node with role=alert; validation itself is the caller's. Destinations are optional throughout — an entry without href renders as a plain unlinked label, matching Header, so an unconfigured footer exposes no empty links.
accessibility.notes: PC only. The footer has a 1024px minimum width. At 1920px the masthead is 50/50 with four link columns; at 1440px it is 50/50 with a two-by-two link grid; at 1024px the link panel is full width above two side-by-side right bands. Below 1024px the page scrolls horizontally; the mobile footer is a separate component.

meta.name: Header
meta.description: YAMI global navigation band. At and above 1024px: brand lockup, storefront hall switcher, locale, deliver-to, search, account / cart, and a category rail whose entries are campaign artwork rather than icon components. Below 1024px it swaps to mobile chrome. The default variant uses a 56px brand bar over a 36px search field; the PDP variant uses a single 56px H5 row with lockup, deliver-to, search, and cart.

figma.notes: PC geometry and token bindings were reconciled against the production www.yami.com/en header at 1480px, because the Figma node was not reachable when this component was built. The default mobile band is measured directly from node 2725:151904. The H5 PDP variant is measured from English Site Optimization 2026 node 2786:18423 (file wE2APma1NxPl3eHM5NFpU9).

mobileVariant.description: Mobile navigation anatomy. pdp renders the single-row, top-sticky H5 PDP header throughout the mobile range below 1024px.

logo.description: Brand lockup artwork. PC renders the assets/logos/yami-ui-<lang>-pc-fill.svg lockup at 52px tall.

mobileLogo.description: Brand lockup below 1024px. Every locale renders assets/logos/yami-ui-en-mobile-fill.svg at 28px tall — a distinct Figma variant with its own mark / wordmark proportions, not the PC file scaled down. Falls back to logo.

darkLogo.description: Brand lockup on dark surfaces. Renders assets/logos/yami-ui-<lang>-pc-fill-inverse.svg — the same locked lockup with a white wordmark, since Fill's #222222 wordmark is invisible on a dark band. Swapped by the .dark class in CSS, not JS. Omit and the band keeps logo in dark mode.

darkMobileLogo.description: Dark-surface counterpart to mobileLogo, from assets/logos/yami-ui-<lang>-mobile-fill-inverse.svg. Omit to keep mobileLogo.

homeHref.description: Destination for the brand lockup. Defaults to the site root.

halls.description: Storefront halls rendered as an inline radiogroup left of the search field (All | Beauty). These scope the storefront, not the search query. EN-only: the CN storefront ships no hall switcher, so omit this there — Header then separates the lockup from the locale / deliver-to group with a rule instead.

hallId.description: Controlled active hall id. Uncontrolled selection falls back to the first hall.

zipcode.description: Deliver-to control beside the locale switcher and before the search field. Omit to hide it.

categories.description: Category rail entries in display order. Each entry's image renders as a 24px , never an icon component; omitting image yields the built-in grid glyph used by the leading Categories entry.

searchPlaceholder.description: Localized placeholder for the query field. Production rotates hot searches through this slot; rotation is the caller's concern.

searchValue.description: Controlled query. Leave undefined for an uncontrolled field.

onSearchSubmit.description: Fires on form submit with the current query.

searchPanel.description: PC search discovery content. Focus with an empty query shows recent, popular, and deal tags; a non-empty query switches to image suggestions.

mobileSearchHref.description: Destination opened when the mobile search field is activated.

onScan.description: Visual search, mobile field only. Omit while the entry is not configured.

account.description: Account entry point. Its label is rendered visibly beside the glyph and is also the accessible name.

locale.description: Country flag artwork rendered at 20px, plus a short locale code such as EN. It lives in the left brand group immediately before deliver-to. Use the maintained DS icons in assets/icons/area/.

cart.description: Cart entry point. The count is folded into the accessible name only — the chrome renders no visible count.

inbox.description: Message centre entry in the mobile brand bar, below 1024px only. The PC band routes messages through the account menu, so this has no desktop counterpart. Omit to hide it.

ariaLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the banner landmark.

hallsLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the hall radiogroup.

categoriesLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the category rail navigation region.

searchLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the search landmark, field, and submit control.

scanLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the mobile field's visual-search control. The control is mobile-only.

nextCategoriesLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the rail's forward paging control.

previousCategoriesLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the rail's backward paging control.

redUsage.note: Category promotion badges are the only red in the chrome and use --text-emphasis. Counts and promotion flags such as NEW qualify; decorative labels do not.

semanticColorOnly.note: No non-semantic hue is baked into the CSS. The band resolves to --surface-primary and exposes no tinting escape hatch.

tapTarget.note: Account, locale, cart, and category entries clear 44px. The 18px hall text controls and the 40px deliver-to control keep their visual size and gain a transparent 44px hit area.

focus.note: Brand, halls, deliver-to, account, locale, cart, category links, rail paging, and the submit button expose a 2px --border-focus outline at 2px offset.

radius.note: Only semantic radius slots. Production's 20px / 16px / 18px pills are all fully-rounded boxes, so they map to --radius-button-primary; focusable text controls use --radius-component-default.

typeHierarchy.note: Three levels in the chrome: link-md (halls, deliver-to, account), body-md (query field), caption-sm (category labels and promotion badges), plus link-sm for the locale code.

numeralsFont.note: The deliver-to postal code and promotion counts inherit --font-family-ios from the header root.

elevationOnPress.note: Hover changes background-color only. The rail paging controls separate from scrolling content with a 1px --border-default ring rather than a shadow, matching production.

noOpacityDisabled.note: Rail paging controls unmount at the boundaries rather than dimming, matching production's display:none, so no disabled styling is required.

borderStrength.note: Production uses #000 for the search ring, 17% black for the cart ring and rail divider, #f5f5f5 for the row rule, and #222 for the closing rule. The DS caps borders at three strengths, so these map to --border-focus, --border-default / --divider-subtle, --border-default, and --divider-emphasis respectively.

--border-focus.selector: .search ring at --stroke-thick; outline-color on every focusable slot

accessibility.role: banner landmark containing a search landmark and a category navigation region
accessibility.ariaPattern: header banner + role=search form with an optional labelled suggestion dialog + nav with a list of category links; halls form an exclusive radiogroup
accessibility.structure: Category artwork carries the category name as alt and repeats it as a visible label. The leading Categories entry uses a decorative glyph and relies on its visible label. The account control shows its label visibly. The locale control names itself via aria-label and hides the short code from assistive technology. The cart folds its item count into aria-label because the chrome shows no visible count.
accessibility.interaction: The PC search panel opens on focus, switches from discovery tags to image suggestions after input, closes on its scrim, submit, or Escape, and leaves mobile unchanged. The category rail scrolls natively; paging controls page by one viewport minus a single anchor entry and unmount at the boundaries. Reduced motion switches paging to immediate scrolling. Promotion badges sit in the category entry's top-right corner and are clipped to one line so a multi-badge entry cannot change the row height.
accessibility.notes: PC only. Below 1024px the rail scrolls rather than reflowing — the mobile header is a separate component.

meta.name: HeroBanner
meta.description: Responsive YAMI homepage campaign rail composed from four explicit content cards: image only, image and text, image text and products, or products only.

items.description: Ordered campaign cards. Their image, copy, and product fields select one of the four public card subcomponents.

ariaLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the campaign region.

previousLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the desktop previous-page button.

nextLabel.description: Localized accessible name for the desktop next-page button.

imageLoading.description: Native loading mode for non-leading campaign images. The first image is always eager/high priority.

dividerPosition.description: Places the optional desktop section boundary above, below, or removes it; ignored below 1024px.

dividerVariant.description: Gray uses the existing 1px structural separator; black uses the theme-aware 2px emphasis separator.

tapTarget.note: Desktop paging composes 36px YAMI icon Buttons whose transparent hit area reaches 44px.

focus.note: Campaign links and paging buttons remain keyboard reachable with visible focus.

radius.note: Campaign cards use --radius-lg (12px); product thumbnails use --radius-md (8px), matching the Figma component.

motion.note: Paging respects prefers-reduced-motion and does not animate card geometry.

gradient.note: The 24px gradient is a functional Figma-specified artwork-to-campaign-surface transition using the sampled bottom-edge image color.

accessibility.role: region containing a list of campaign links
accessibility.ariaPattern: labelled region with list/listitem campaign links and optional paging buttons
accessibility.structure: Campaign images require semantic alt text. Image-only cards use the image alt as the link accessible name.
accessibility.interaction: Mobile uses native horizontal scrolling. Desktop paging buttons reuse ProductList rail navigation and disable at boundaries, while the progress track and aria-live count report how many banners have been revealed through the current viewport against the total banner count.

meta.name: HorizontalScrollList
meta.description: Polymorphic finite horizontal list with native scrolling, hidden scrollbars, item snapping, and a shared controller hook for paging controls.

as.description: Semantic element rendered for the list, commonly div, ul, or ol.

enabled.description: Applies the horizontal scrolling behavior and default keyboard focusability.

surface.description: Selects a transparent square rail over the caller background or a plain rail. Both surfaces use 8px item and edge spacing on mobile.

children.description: List items. Callers own item width and scroll-snap alignment.

nativeScrolling.note: Finite rails use native horizontal scrolling; callers do not translate the list with transforms.

itemGeometry.note: The list owns scrolling while callers own item width, gap, and edge padding.

accessibility.role: caller-owned list semantics
accessibility.ariaPattern: list
accessibility.notes: Enabled lists default to tabIndex=0. Callers must provide an accessible label and semantic list items.

meta.name: Input
meta.description: YAMI Input Field from Figma `↪ 表单输入 Forms`. Responsive single-line native input with embedded label, value row, clear action, helper/error supporting text, and accessible form semantics.

label.description: Embedded field label rendered inside the control.

helperText.description: Supporting text below the input. Hidden when error is present.

error.description: Error supporting text. Sets aria-invalid, role='alert', and attention border.

state.description: Visual state override for catalog demos. Product usage normally derives state from value/focus/error/disabled.

clearable.description: Shows the clear-fill action while focus remains inside the field and the input has a value.

meta.name: Tabs
meta.description: Navigation tabs for switching between related content panes. Implements YAMI Primary Style A/B, Secondary, and Tertiary variants from the YAMI UI UX Guidelines Tabs node, with default and inverse surfaces plus ARIA tab behavior.

figma.notes: Tabs source node `↪ 选项卡 Tabs`. Figma splits Mobile and WEB component sets and splits Primary Style A/B into separate sets. Code keeps one compound component with variant/styleVariant/inverse props and responsive CSS. Icon slots exist in WEB button components but are disabled in the reference examples; code exposes leftIcon/rightIcon for product use with real YAMI SVG assets.
figma.sizeDelta: Mobile Primary Style A uses 56px list height and 18/24 text; WEB Primary uses 48px and 16/20. Mobile Primary Style B uses a 52px segmented surface with 32px visible selected pill inside a 44px hit target. Secondary stays underline-based at 44px on both mobile and PC. Tertiary uses 48px triggers and hit targets with 32px selected pills vertically centered inside.
figma.stateMapping: Figma State=Default/Skeleton maps to TabsList skeleton=false/true. Selected/default tab states map to data-state='active'/'inactive'. Hover/focus are code-only interaction states; disabled is a code-side accessibility state for product use.

notes: Use TabsList as the direct trigger container and TabsTrigger for each tab option.
Use TabsContent when tab panels differ. Match every TabsTrigger value to a TabsContent value.
Do not replace triggers with plain buttons or custom spans.
